title: poa nemoralis subsp. vulgaris
intro: Poa nemoralis subsp. vulgaris, commonly known as common meadow-grass, is a subspecies of grass that belongs to the family Poaceae. It is native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa, and is often found growing in grasslands, meadows, and along roadsides. Poa nemoralis subsp. vulgaris has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, with potential health benefits including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are thought to contribute to its therapeutic actions, including sedative and antispasmodic effects.
